title: Weak hyperbolic normal criterion and transverse reflection
reviewed_arguments: The full NC1 weak form retains time-variable positive spatial coefficients, face-zero cross block, arbitrary complex lower matrices, actual Banach-adjoint normal terms and both H1/H1_0 domains on a fixed compact patch.
HN8–HN12 retain every lower term and opposite normal-factor position. HN26a uses the actual real symmetric coefficient array; no non-Hermitian boundary functional is dropped.
HN14–HN16 retain all time derivatives and both tau signs. The hyperbolic scale is large epsilon followed by small delta, with a full incoming cap and separated normal cutoff derivatives.

The radial regularizer is legal on both spaces, including lacunary residuals. HN22 keeps the exact amplitude/derivative ratio; HN23–HN25 retain the weight derivatives and globally normalized error symbols.
The complete ordered HN26 decomposition retains the principal characteristic multiple as a weak form. Lower and incoming arrays are balanced at their exact mean orders.
The coarse companion reuses only the weak spatial coercivity proof, not glancing smallness. It proves every order-minus-one normal commutator and exact normalized normal bound.

The new mean-order norm argument proves the square-root remainder at energy order s-1/2. HN33–HN38 retain all three normal-parametrix tails, opposite lower-form factors and the corrected left half-order source parametrix.
HN37–HN38 preserve the sharp natural-dual forcing index s+1 and the actual minus residual. HN39 explicitly absorbs geometry, weight, complex lower form and all eleven Young terms.
HN40 identifies limits by the actual supported operator action on tests reaching the boundary. No H1 zero extension is assumed; the Dirichlet subspace is closed.
HN42 retains one common positive-cutoff neighborhood for every order. Variable analytic constants never shrink its fixed geometric region.

The geometry companion proves separated lifts, unique cap hitting, a whole incoming half-neighborhood filled by the full interior matrix propagation theorem, outgoing propagation, both clock directions and a common smooth flow box. Its analytic dependencies are acyclic.
HN45 checks the exact Lorentzian density and Hermitian bundle factors. The Vasy framework is credited without importing its selfadjoint commutator equality for the general complex form.

All 51 receiving obligations, 71 displays, 57 original labels, five complete solutions, both lesson figures and the complete illustrated geometry/coarse companions remain. The final exercise uses exact Fourier, ordinary elliptic and conormal providers, including its nonunitary matrix inverse.
Six finite model groups with 96 cases supplement the complete proofs. All 634 formulas and 70 numbered displays across three readers render; all 35 final captures were inspected.
